## Grammar

Basic word order is SOV; it has postpositions. In the noun phrase: possessor before the possessed; noun before the adjective; demonstrative before the noun; noun before the numeral; relative clause before the noun. Overall it is head-final.
It has a definite article before the noun, an indefinite article, no case marking on nouns, nominative-accusative alignment, singular and plural, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark perfective and habitual; there is an indirect (reported or inferred) evidential. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use intonation alone. Verbs agree with the subject by suffixes; not with the object.
Other features: pronouns can be dropped; serial verbs; verb reduplication; a copula; a periphrastic causative; no passive; question words left in place; a decimal counting base; a 'have' verb for possession.
Measured morphology: 10 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 0.9 (0 free word … 3 fused), 8 paradigm cells, 1 of them with allomorphy.
